analyses.summary: On the project's own pre-registered logic, the dev results literally block the pipeline. E1 fails: only 11/15 O seeds have agreement with their own teacher above the best other teacher. e1_plan §0 says that means 'fix training first, do not enter E2 / E3', so E3 is blocked too, not just E2. E2 on dev lands in the 'none pass' row of the e2_plan §2 table (0/3), which would demote RQ1 to exploratory and move the main line to E2b/E3/E4/E5. The failure is not the one the E1 rule was written to catch. Students learned their teachers: they reproduce their own teacher's training labels 98.5-99.5% of the time. The cause is that the teachers barely differ at the label level, and the student's base model already looks like DeepSeek. My exploratory checks (dev only, not pre-registered) show three things. (1) The one near-pass, DeepSeek's Δρ = +0.182, is explained by the base. The untrained base S_0 (with the 0.9 mass rule relaxed) already correlates 0.533 with DeepSeek on the same 139 families; the DeepSeek student reaches 0.504. Partialling out S_0 sends all three Δρ toward 0, with every CI including 0. (2) A teacher-centred comparison flips the picture: students of teacher T are closer to T than the other teachers' students are. The contrast is +0.103 for GPT-4o, +0.069 for Claude and +0.097 for DeepSeek (CIs exclude 0 for GPT-4o and DeepSeek), the grid permutation gives p < 1e-4, and a label-free nearest-teacher classifier gets 13/15 right versus 5/15 for the pre-registered student-centred one. (3) Suggestibility, a quantity the plan names but attaches no threshold to, carries over in teacher order: the base starts at 0.166, and students land at 0.168 / 0.121 / 0.051 for teachers at 0.140 / 0.077 / 0.056. Students move away from the base roughly in proportion to how far their teacher sits below it. The evidence therefore matches neither row of the docs/01 §6 'can say' table cleanly. Supported: the size of the polarity-suggestibility type effect is passed on, anchored by the base prior; each student is shifted toward its own teacher relative to the other students. Not supported: 'the student's profile is more like its own teacher than like other teachers', which is the pre-registered RQ1 as written.

findings.title: E1 rule, read literally: fails and also gates E3
findings.detail: e1_plan §0 / docs/03 §0: every student's agreement with its own teacher must exceed its agreement with each other teacher, 'otherwise fix training first, do not enter E2 / E3'. Dev result: 11/15 seeds pass (deepseek_v4 5/5, claude46 4/5, gpt4o 2/5 with one exact tie). The stated purpose of the rule is to catch 'not learned' (e2_plan §2: 'otherwise E2's rho just means it did not learn'). Diagnostics show learning happened: 98.5-99.5% reproduction of training labels, and 90-97% siding with their own teacher on training items where two teachers disagree. The failure comes from low label-level distinctness: training labels agree 93.3-95.8% pairwise, and gpt4o vs DeepSeek differ on only 198/4,734 items. Applying E1 strictly blocks E3 as well. Proceeding requires a documented deviation, i.e. a post hoc reinterpretation of a pre-registered gate.
findings.evidence: tasks/e1_plan.md §0, §3; results/e1_dev/summary.md (E1 decision block, agreement table); tasks/hpc_log.md 2026-10-04 diagnostics 1-2; results/e1_dev_diag/train_label_reproduction.txt (via hpc_log)

With 300 test families the DeepSeek CI will narrow, so the most plausible test outcome is 'partial' (1 teacher, which hands the headline to E3) or 'none'. A 'partial' pass driven by DeepSeek would be uninterpretable as inheritance (next finding). Two of the three e2_plan §2 control conditions cannot be met as written. E1 has not passed. 'S_0's Δρ ≈ 0' is undefined: S_0 belongs to no teacher, and under the 0.9 rule only 6 families are complete. Its spirit (the base should not already resemble a teacher) is violated under the relaxed rule.

findings.title: The base prior explains DeepSeek's near-pass (exploratory)
findings.detail: On the same 139 complete families, S_0 with the 0.9 rule relaxed correlates 0.533 with DeepSeek, 0.277 with GPT-4o and 0.245 with Claude. The seed-pooled DeepSeek student reaches 0.504 with DeepSeek, so it does not move toward DeepSeek relative to the base (move -0.029, CI [-0.131, 0.069]). Change from base toward the own teacher: GPT-4o student +0.100 [-0.014, 0.219]; Claude student -0.011 [-0.153, 0.122]. Partial ρ controlling for the S_0 profile gives Δρ gpt4o +0.020 [-0.146, 0.182], claude46 -0.022 [-0.194, 0.100], deepseek_v4 +0.086 [-0.056, 0.231]. Removing each model's own type effects δ(j) (residual profile) gives -0.023 / -0.052 / +0.134 [-0.015, 0.282]. Every S_0-based number uses the relaxed mass rule: S_0 is 75% malformed under the protocol, so treat it as diagnostic only.

findings.title: Teacher-centred (column-wise) evidence of transmission is positive (exploratory, but the grid permutation is pre-specified)
findings.detail: The pre-registered Δρ is student-centred: is the student closer to its own teacher than to other teachers? That comparison is confounded by teacher reliability (rel_T 0.675 / 0.383 / 0.515) and by the base's resemblance to each teacher. Holding the teacher fixed cancels both. The question becomes whether S_T is closer to T than S_T' is. Contrast ρ(S_T,T) − mean ρ(S_T',T): gpt4o +0.103 [0.031, 0.182], claude46 +0.069 [-0.036, 0.163], deepseek_v4 +0.097 [0.008, 0.185]. The grid permutation (teacher labels shuffled across the 15 runs) gives observed mean Δρ -0.005 against a null mean of -0.081 (SD 0.017), p < 1e-4. Status of that test: docs/03 §3 lists 'shuffle the students' teacher assignment ... 10,000 times' as a planned permutation, but it is not the decision criterion. Nearest-teacher classification on per-run ρ: student-centred argmax 5/15 (everyone goes to DeepSeek, i.e. chance); label-free leave-one-run-out column-centred 13/15; agreement-based argmax 11/15. These classifiers are post hoc. Column centring assumes a balanced closed set of students.
findings.evidence: results/e1_dev/grid_permutation.json; results/e1_dev/inheritance.csv rho__ columns; my inline computations (move_from_base.out teacher-wise contrast; nearest-teacher counts printed in session)

findings.title: Suggestibility carries over in teacher order and is the strongest positive signal (quantity pre-specified, no threshold)
findings.detail: δ(T5)−δ(T6): teachers DeepSeek 0.140 > GPT-4o 0.077 > Claude 0.056. Students 0.168 > 0.121 > 0.051 (seed SD ≤ 0.014). R students 0.001; S_0 relaxed 0.166. From the base, the GPT-4o student drops 0.045 and the Claude student 0.115, toward their teachers' levels; the DeepSeek student stays at the base level, so its 'match' is not distinguishable from base. Status: e2_plan §0/§1 names suggestibility inheritance and order preservation as a quantity, and the 'none pass' row says to report its direction anyway. docs/E0_results §9 even called suggestibility the clear, powered form of RQ1, with cell-level residual correlation as secondary. The frozen e2_plan §2 rule, however, uses cell-level Δρ. So the two pre-training documents disagree on what is primary. Limitations: only 3 teacher points (chance of matching the order is 1/6), and the base reference uses the relaxed rule.
findings.evidence: results/e1_dev_diag/dev_suggestibility_base_profile.txt; tasks/e2_plan.md §0-§2; docs/E0_results.md §9 ('RQ1 有了明确、可学、有 power 的形态... cell 级残差相关作为次级检验')

findings.title: Reliability ceiling
findings.detail: Teacher order split-half reliability (Spearman-Brown corrected), quoted from docs. Pilot v2: GPT-4o 0.726, Claude 0.357 (cross-pass retest 0.997), DeepSeek 0.627. Dev: 0.675 / 0.383 (retest 0.993) / 0.515, which I recomputed exactly. Test (teacher side, quoted): 0.691 / 0.329 (retest 0.990) / 0.466. Student reliability on dev, which I computed: between-seed profile r 0.886 / 0.791 / 0.888 for gpt4o / claude46 / deepseek_v4, Spearman-Brown to 5 seeds 0.975 / 0.950 / 0.975; seed-pooled order split-half 0.935 / 0.839 / 0.929. Pooled ρ_own 0.377 / 0.234 / 0.504. The plan's ratio ρ/rel_T: 0.558 / 0.611 / 0.979. Classical attenuation ceiling sqrt(rel_T·rel_S): 0.811 / 0.603 / 0.709. Disattenuated ρ_own: 0.465 / 0.388 / 0.711. Disattenuation does not rescue Δρ: disattenuated ρ to DeepSeek is 0.662 for the GPT-4o student and 0.493 for the Claude student, both above their own-teacher values. The DeepSeek student sits at its ceiling, but so does the untrained base (0.533). Methodological note: e2_plan §4 says Claude's ρ_own 'cannot exceed about 0.33'. That conflates reliability with the correlation ceiling, which is sqrt(rel_T·rel_S) ≈ 0.57 on test if rel_S ≈ 1. And for Claude the order split-half measures order-specific but deterministic signal (retest 0.99), not sampling noise. It is still the relevant ceiling for learnability, because training keeps only order-stable items (stable_one), which removes that order-specific signal.
findings.evidence: docs/E0_results.md §9, §13; tasks/e2_plan.md §1, §4; /hai/scratch/tomyyc/vcd_diag/wf/claims_mapper/rel_ceiling.out

findings.title: Premises P1-P3
findings.detail: P1 (teachers answer): holds; answer rate ≥ 99%. P2 (teacher profiles systematic, reliable, distinct): holds at the type level (T6 negative for all teachers; suggestibility spans a 2.5-5x range) and at the profile level (residual correlation 0.17-0.34 dev, 0.20-0.28 test). Two weak spots. (i) Reliability: the E0 gate 'two or more teachers with reliability < 0.5 means P2 fails' was applied on the pilot, where of the chosen three only Claude failed. On the test-set teacher numbers already in docs, Claude 0.329 and DeepSeek 0.466 are both below 0.5, so the literal gate would trip there. (ii) The distinctness the design checked was profile distinctness; E1 needs judgment-level distinctness, which is low (majority agreement 0.83-0.89 dev, 0.90-0.92 test; training labels 93-96%). The base resembling DeepSeek is a new premise failure the design did not anticipate: the student's prior is not neutral across teachers. P3 (rewriter preserves content): F passes both auditors (v9: 97.3% / 93.3%); C is contested (97.3% vs 74.7%; κ ≈ 0). Not touched by the E1/E2 results, but relevant to E3.
findings.evidence: docs/01_related_work.md §5; docs/03_experiments.md §1 gate table; docs/E0_results.md §2, §9, §11 (v9), §13; results/e1_dev_diag

findings.title: RQs and contributions affected
findings.detail: RQ1 (heritability): as pre-registered (student-centred Δρ) it is not supported on dev; partial support in teacher-centred form plus the suggestibility magnitude. RQ4 (provenance, E7): weakened. A ρ-based nearest teacher with the student-centred rule scores 5/15 (chance) on dev; a label-free centred variant scores 13/15, but that is post hoc. RQ2 (data origin, E2b) and RQ3 (form modulation, E3): not directly affected; docs/01 §5 already says that if P2 fails, RQ2 and RQ3 can still be done. C1 (controlled evidence on Moore's open question): weakened in its strong form, but can be reframed as 'the type-level disposition transmits, and the student's base prior anchors the family-level profile'. C2 (typed-framing benchmark and frontier profiles): intact. C3 / C4 (form modulation, mechanism): intact, pending E3. C5 (behavioural provenance through style laundering): weakest, since it depends on RQ1 and RQ4.
findings.evidence: docs/01_related_work.md §5-§6; computations above

findings.title: Which row of the docs/01 §6 can-say table
findings.detail: Neither row fits cleanly. Row 1 ('profile systematic and inherited') holds only for the type-level component: the suggestibility magnitude and teacher ordering. Row 2 ('profile systematic but not inherited: the student's inconsistency is its own') fits the family-level profile measured student-centred: after partialling S_0 or removing type effects, no Δρ excludes 0, and every student is closest to DeepSeek, as the base already is. The teacher-centred contrast, though, says teacher-specific information does shift each student. The defensible statement is a third row the table lacks: the student's profile equals its base prior plus a teacher-modulated type effect plus a small teacher-specific family-level shift that is detectable only relative to other teachers' students. The 'cannot say' column still applies: no claim about internal values, and no claim that other scales also fail to transmit.
findings.evidence: docs/01_related_work.md §6 table; findings above

findings.title: Which downstream experiments stay meaningful if RQ1 is weak
findings.detail: E2b (RQ2): fully meaningful. It is a within-teacher contrast (consistent vs inconsistent demonstrations) judged against the seed null, needs no teacher distinctness, and the base prior is constant across arms. The suggestibility result supports its premise that framing dispositions are learnable from demonstrations. Seed nulls are small: flip-rate SD ≤ 0.009, agreement SD ≤ 0.008. E3 (RQ3): parts (a) judgment change and (b) consistency change are measured relative to S_{T,O}, seed-paired, so they stay well-defined and sensitive. Suggestibility change (seed SD ≤ 0.014) is also a sensitive outcome. Part (c), change in inheritance Δρ(S_{T,F/C}) − Δρ(S_{T,O}), inherits the base-prior confound and is noisy (Δρ seed-null SD 0.033, q95 0.095). ρ_own changes or the teacher-centred contrast would be cleaner, but those are post hoc. E3 is the pre-registered fallback headline (e2_plan §2), but the E1 gate also blocks it, so a deviation note is needed. E4 (mechanism): meaningful only if E3 shows an effect. H3 (S_0 perplexity) becomes more interesting given the base-prior finding. E5 (fix): runnable, but its 'no homogenisation / distinctness preserved' acceptance has little room when baseline student distinctness is small (student agreement own ≈ other). E7: as specified (nearest teacher by ρ), it currently runs at chance on dev and would need a pre-frozen centred classifier.
findings.evidence: docs/03_experiments.md §0, §4-§7; results/e1_dev/summary.md seed-noise table; tasks/e2_plan.md §2, §5

findings.title: The power check promised in docs/04 §3 is not on record
findings.detail: docs/04 §3 requires a simulation from pilot variances confirming power ≥ 0.8 for Δρ = 0.1 with 5 seeds × 300 families. I found no record of it in docs/ or tasks/. The dev Δρ seed-null SD (0.033) and the family-bootstrap CI half-widths (about 0.13-0.15 on 139 families) suggest that Δρ = 0.1 would be borderline on test even without the base confound.

analyses.implications: For an ACL/EMNLP main submission: the pre-registered headline (RQ1 as student-centred Δρ on ≥ 2/3 teachers) will very likely fail on test, or 'pass' only for DeepSeek in a way the base prior explains. Leading with 'inconsistency is heritable' is not supportable from these data. Several findings are still publishable if framed honestly. (1) The type-level disposition (polarity suggestibility) transmits through SFT in teacher order, and students move from the base toward their teacher's level. That is a concrete, controlled, partial answer to Moore et al.'s open question. (2) A methodological result: the natural criterion 'the student resembles its own teacher more than other teachers' is confounded by the student's base prior and by teacher reliability. Teacher-centred comparisons show transmission that student-centred ones miss. This matters for provenance and fingerprinting work too. (3) E2b and E3 remain clean within-teacher experiments with small seed nulls, and e2_plan §2 already names E3 as the fallback headline. Process requirements. Any new metric (partial-on-S_0, residualised Δρ, teacher-centred contrast, suggestibility threshold) must be chosen and frozen on dev before test, written up as a declared deviation in tasks/hpc_log.md or e0_plan, and reported next to the failed pre-registered rule, never in place of it. The E1 gate must be explicitly reinterpreted, since it literally blocks E3. The S_0 reference should be measured without relaxing the protocol: for example a few-shot or format-only control student; the R students partly play that role but carry no profile. Without that, every base-prior argument rests on a relaxed-rule diagnostic. Options (a) and (b) from the HPC log are compatible: run test once with the frozen original rule plus pre-frozen secondary analyses. Option (c), retraining or changing the base, changes the experiment and resets the pre-registration.
open_questions: Is the base-prior resemblance to DeepSeek robust under a protocol-compliant S_0 reference (for example a few-shot base or a format-only SFT student with neutral rationales), rather than the relaxed 0.9 rule on a model that is 75% malformed?
Does the T0 (unseen framing) Δρ or teacher-centred contrast behave differently? The dev E2 analysis used only T1/T3/T5/T6, and e2_plan §4 calls T0 the cleanest evidence.

By-variant pattern (per seed, not pooled): GPT-4o students have positive Δρ on T5 in 5/5 seeds; DeepSeek students' advantage sits on T1/T3, not T5/T6. Is this a real type-specific inheritance signature or noise?
Should the Mac side freeze a secondary E2 criterion now (teacher-centred contrast or S_0-partial Δρ, with a threshold), and a threshold for suggestibility order and size, before the single test run?

Would order_policy 'both', which keeps contested and order-unstable items, raise label-level teacher distinctness enough to make E1's student-centred rule informative? That is option (c), with a new pre-registration.
Is the E1 gate on E3 meant to apply when the failure comes from low teacher distinctness rather than failed training? This needs an explicit Mac-side ruling.

analyses.summary: Everything here is exploratory: dev only, not pre-registered, and no test file was opened. Three results stand out. (1) The pre-registered row test (is the student closest to its own teacher?) fails for structural reasons, not for lack of power. The untrained base already resembles DeepSeek: partial-out Pearson with DeepSeek is 0.533 on the 139 analysis families, versus 0.28 for GPT-4o and 0.25 for Claude. The family-permutation null also keeps each teacher's type effects, so its mean depends on the teacher: −0.094 for the GPT-4o student, −0.090 for Claude, +0.088 for DeepSeek. If the dev estimates are the true values, the pre-registered E2 rule passes on test with probability about 0.05 (simulation). (2) Asked the other way round (does a teacher's profile match its own student better than the other students?), inheritance is clear and robust. The diagonal-minus-off-diagonal interaction of the 3x3 student-by-teacher matrix is positive under all 8 versions I tried: raw r, r with the base S0 partialled out, r with the teacher mean partialled out, type-effect residuals, distillation gain against the teacher-unique component, and per-family suggestibility. Values run 0.09 to 0.19, with within-family label-permutation p ≤ 0.005 in every case. It is also positive for all 5 seeds taken one at a time. Column deltas for single teachers are mostly positive, but only Claude (and DeepSeek on some versions) clears Holm. (3) There is no detectable inheritance on the unseen paraphrase framing T0 (interaction 0.026, p 0.20), and T0 is underpowered. For ACL this is useful but means reframing the claim. The defensible claim is a causal, relative one: which teacher a student was trained on shifts its framing profile toward that teacher. This sits on top of a large shared base prior. 'Each student's profile is closest to its own teacher' does not hold. Using the column / interaction test as the confirmatory one requires freezing a single primary statistic on dev before test runs (option (b)). Its projected power on test is high: MDE80 about 0.05 to 0.06 against dev values of 0.09 to 0.10.

findings.title: The pre-registered family-permutation null is not centred on 0 and depends on the teacher
findings.detail: Permuting student families keeps the variant structure, so it keeps the shared type effects (T5 > 0, T6 < 0). Null means for the row delta are −0.094 (gpt4o student), −0.090 (claude46) and +0.088 (deepseek_v4). DeepSeek's large suggestibility therefore raises its own bar. On type-effect-residualized shifts (each model's own variant means removed) all three null means become about −0.03. Residualized row deltas are −0.023 (p 0.46), −0.052 (p 0.69) and +0.134 (p 0.003).

With S0 + rbar partialled out: 0.054 (p 0.14), 0.182 (Holm p 0.003), 0.092 (Holm p 0.064). Gain against the teacher-unique component: 0.062 (p 0.10), 0.171 (Holm 0.002), 0.191 (Holm 0.002).

findings.title: (c) Agreement gain over the base is small, and own-teacher specificity is weak
findings.detail: On the same 139 families (seen variants), S0_relaxed already agrees 0.795 / 0.784 / 0.824 with gpt4o / claude46 / deepseek_v4. Gain from training with the own teacher: gpt4o student +0.063, claude46 student +0.070, deepseek_v4 student +0.038. Row gain (own gain minus best other gain): +0.0001 [−0.027, 0.022], +0.035 [−0.008, 0.082], −0.009 [−0.052, 0.022]. Column gain: +0.028 (label-perm p 0.017), +0.008 (p 0.20), −0.010 (p 0.60). On the 105 contested cells, column agreement is clear only for Claude: +0.177 [0.019, 0.294], p 0.001. analyses.implications: What the dev data support (exploratory): training teacher identity causally shifts the student's framing profile toward that teacher. Training data is the only manipulated variable, and label-permutation tests that hold the base and the teachers fixed show it. Mean-level suggestibility is inherited with its ordering preserved, and training largely overrides the base level (Claude student 0.048 vs base 0.165). The effect is small next to the shared base prior and the shared type effects. Raw student-teacher rho is 0.14 to 0.50, and base agreement with the teachers is already 0.78 to 0.82. That is a legitimate pre-registered null, and the paper can still report the grid permutation, suggestibility and shared R² as e2_plan §2 already allows. (2) Option (b) is supportable: a base-controlled, column-wise or interaction test with label permutation is better aligned with the causal question and well powered on test. Pick one primary statistic, not the best of the 8 here, because the forking-paths risk is real (proposal: interaction on raw r or on r with S0 partialled out, label permutation, plus per-teacher column deltas as secondary with Holm). (3) The confounds found here (a DeepSeek-like base prior, a permutation null that keeps type effects and so has teacher-dependent means, teacher calibration in JSD, 93 to 96% overlap in teacher labels) are a methodological contribution in their own right for teacher-attribution and 'subliminal or trait transfer' style claims. They argue for always reporting a base-model control and a student-swap null. (4) Before relying on a single-teacher column test, note that only the Claude column is consistently significant, so 'all three teachers' heritability' is not supported on dev.

audits.reasoning:
EXPLORATORY (dev only, not pre-registered). I rebuilt the pooled (5-seed mean) family-demeaned profiles on 139 complete dev families from the raw dev_responses and teacher dev profiles, using my own permutation, bootstrap and MDE code. The observed pooled delta_rho matches results/e1_dev/inheritance_pooled.csv: -0.111 (claude46), +0.182 (deepseek_v4), -0.092 (gpt4o).

The arithmetic reproduces. I used thr_test = null_mean + z(1-a) * null_sd/sqrt(2) and MDE80 = thr_test + 0.84 * boot_se/sqrt(2), with a = 0.05/3. That gives 0.024 (gpt4o), 0.044 (claude46) and 0.198 (deepseek_v4). The claim says 0.024 / 0.048 / 0.196. The claude46 gap (0.044 vs 0.048) is because the other analyst's power.py takes the empirical 98.33% quantile of the null instead of a normal approximation; the null has a right tail. The deepseek gap is Monte Carlo noise.

The "structural null mean" assumption holds. The family permutation shuffles student rows but keeps the per-variant (type-effect) column means, so the expected null correlation is n * sum_j sbar_j tbar_j / norms, which does not depend on n. My analytic structural delta0 values (-0.087 / +0.095 / -0.094) almost equal the permutation null means (-0.091 / +0.089 / -0.095). In half-size subsamples (n = 70, 100 replicates) the null mean stays the same (-0.096 / +0.082 / -0.096), while the null SD grows by about sqrt(2) (claude46 0.060 -> 0.084). So keeping the mean and scaling only the spread is right, and letting the small noise part of the mean shrink changes the MDE by 0.002 or less.

Where the claim falls short as a statement about the pre-registered rule:
(1) The E2 rule requires pooled delta_rho > 0 as well as Holm p < 0.05. For gpt4o the Holm threshold on test is about -0.020, so delta > 0 is the binding condition. The effective MDE80 is then about 0 + 0.84 * 0.052 = 0.044, not 0.024. For claude46 the threshold is about 0, so its value is about 0.045 either way. power.py reports p(delta_hat > 0) and uses it in its rule simulation, but the MDE row ignores it.
(2) The projection reuses the dev null mean for test. On test the null mean is recomputed from the test type effects. Its family-bootstrap SD at test size is 0.011–0.014, so each MDE has roughly ±0.02–0.03 uncertainty that the claim does not mention.
(3) It assumes n_test / n_dev = 2 complete families (300 vs 150 in the docs; the 139 complete on dev suggests about 278 on test). The exact count is not verifiable without opening test files, which is forbidden.
(4) a = 0.0167 is only the first Holm step. Under the ">= 2/3 teachers" rule the second teacher is tested at 0.025, which gives a normal-approximation MDE of 0.037 for claude46 (0.045 once delta > 0 is imposed). So the claim's alpha is conservative.

Substantive reading, which stays robust: deepseek_v4 needs a test delta of about 0.20, close to its dev point estimate of 0.182. Power if the true value equals the dev estimate is about 0.68 at a = 0.0167. gpt4o and claude46 would each need a sign reversal from about -0.1 to about +0.045, with power around 0.02–0.04 if dev is representative.
alternative_explanations: The claim's numbers may be meant as the MDE for the Holm permutation test alone, not the full pre-registered rule. Read that way, gpt4o 0.024 is right; read as the rule (which also requires delta > 0), it understates by about 0.02.

The claude46 difference (0.048 claimed vs 0.044 mine) comes from the threshold method (empirical quantile vs normal approximation), not an error. Both are defensible; the empirical quantile is slightly more faithful to the skewed null of the max-based statistic.

Test type effects (teacher and student delta(T5)-delta(T6)) could differ from dev. That would move the structural null mean and therefore every MDE, especially deepseek_v4, whose threshold of about 0.16 is mostly structural.

audits.reasoning:
EXPLORATORY (dev only, not pre-registered). I recomputed the numbers from scratch: raw JSON, my own symmetrisation, majority-act agreement on T1/T3/T5/T6 with ties at 0.5 dropped, and S0_relaxed using every base row that has p_letters. My student-vs-own-teacher seed means match the official results (0.856, 0.846, 0.844). Each 'gain' is a student's agreement with a teacher minus S0_relaxed's agreement with that same teacher. The 'own-specific row gain' is the gain with the own teacher minus the largest gain with another teacher, i.e. E1 adjusted for the base model.

Restricted to the analyst's 139 families (those complete for all teachers, runs and S0), I reproduce the claim exactly. Own gains are gpt4o +0.0626, claude46 +0.0701, deepseek_v4 +0.0385. Row-specific gains are gpt4o +0.0001 (0.0626 minus 0.0625 vs claude46) and deepseek_v4 -0.0089 (0.0385 minus 0.0473 vs claude46).

Three problems:
(1) The claim leaves out claude46, whose row-specific gain is +0.035 (+0.0352 on the 139 families, +0.0355 on all cells). It is positive in all 5 seeds (0.013 to 0.050), so 'own-specific row gains are about 0' holds for 2 of 3 teachers, not all three.
(2) On all available cells rather than the 139-family subset, the own-gain range is +0.032 to +0.070 (deepseek 0.0323), not +0.038, and gpt4o's row-specific gain is -0.0026.
(3) 'About 0' is only a point estimate. Family-bootstrap 95% CIs are wide: gpt4o [-0.029, 0.022], deepseek [-0.048, 0.025], claude46 [-0.006, 0.081]. Per-seed gpt4o values range from -0.015 to +0.008.

Alternative explanations I checked:
- The relaxed readout is not artefact-prone. The base's letter mass is 0.70 to 0.95 (median 0.88), so the 0.9 rule rejects it only narrowly, and gains are identical for mass thresholds from 0 to 0.5.
- Under the strict 0.9 rule, S0 keeps only 112 cells. On those, S0 agreement is 0.83 to 0.86 and the own gains become -0.061 (gpt4o), -0.027 (claude46) and +0.021 (deepseek). The baseline therefore depends on which cells are kept, though the 112 cells are a small, selected subset.
- S0_relaxed already agrees most with DeepSeek (0.812, vs 0.794 for GPT-4o and 0.776 for Claude). Gains toward DeepSeek are therefore mechanically smaller, which is consistent with the base-prior explanation.

Overall: the arithmetic is correct on the stated cell set, but the summary 'own-specific gains about 0' is selective (it drops claude46 at +0.035) and the low end of the range depends on the cell set.
alternative_explanations: Cell-set choice: on the 139-family common set the own gains are 0.038 to 0.070; on all cells they are 0.032 to 0.070, and gpt4o's row-specific gain changes from +0.0001 to -0.0026.

Base-prior asymmetry: S0_relaxed already agrees most with DeepSeek (0.812, vs 0.794 GPT-4o and 0.776 Claude). This caps DeepSeek gains, so row-specific gains for students whose closest other teacher is DeepSeek or Claude reflect the base's starting point, not only what was learned from the teacher.

Mass-threshold dependence: S0 under the strict 0.9 rule (112 cells) already reaches 0.83 to 0.86 agreement, which turns the gpt4o and claude own gains negative on those cells. The relaxed baseline itself looks benign (letter mass median 0.88).

Ceiling: teachers agree with each other 0.83 to 0.96, so the base-adjusted gains have little room to separate own from other teachers. The 'about 0' is within the noise (bootstrap CI half-widths 0.025 to 0.045), not evidence of zero.

Row-specific gain (own minus max other), all cells: gpt4o -0.0026, claude46 +0.0355, deepseek -0.0089.

analyses.summary:
简短结论（探索性，dev 上，非预注册）：按原头条 F1（'不一致可以遗传'）写论文，现在的结果撑不住。预注册的 E2 是 0/3，E1 只部分通过。grid permutation 的 p<1e-4 说明学生的 profile 带有自己 teacher 的痕迹，但效应很小。不过这组结果放进文献里，恰好落在一个空位上，对冲 ACL 是有益的。

已有工作的情况：subliminal learning 只在 teacher 和 student 共享 base 时传递（Cloud et al. 2507.14805 / Nature 2026），在全量微调下可能还会消失（2606.00831，有争议）。phantom transfer（2602.04899）表明低维、方向性的 trait 可以跨家族传，通过语义线索。sycophancy 可以从训练数据学到，也能用数据改掉（Sharma ICLR 2024；Wei 2308.03958）。fine-tune 后的模型会回到预训练分布（Ji et al. ACL 2025 Best Paper）。

我们的 dev 数字与这些都一致，并且往前推了一步：
- 低维的 suggestibility 按 teacher 顺序传递：Claude 学生从基座的 0.166 降到 0.051，teacher 是 0.056。
- teacher 特有的逐题、逐 framing 判断几乎不传。
- 学生在未见题上的敏感性结构由基座先验主导：所有学生最接近的都是 DeepSeek，而基座本身就像 DeepSeek。
- agreement、Δρ、JSD 被基座先验和 teacher 校准混淆。

建议的主线是 F2（跨家族蒸馏里，传过去的是什么），把 F3（混淆与 base-controlled 指标）作为方法贡献，F1 作为未通过的预注册假设如实报告。F2 的新意我判断为中高，F3 中等。F2 最大的风险是审稿人说 '三个 teacher 太像，是 power 问题'，需要第二个基座和保留争议项的训练来回应。

findings.title: Subliminal learning：跨 base 不传递；我们的设定排除了这条通道，结果与之一致
findings.detail: Cloud et al.（arXiv 2507.14805，2025；正式版发表在 Nature 2026，s41586-026-10319-8）的摘要原文是 'we do not observe the effect when the teacher and student have different base models'（例如 GPT-4.1 nano 的数据传给 GPT-4.1 nano 学生，不传给 Qwen2.5 学生）。Blank et al.（arXiv 2606.00995，2026）认为机制是一个 steering vector，并且需要自适应优化器。Nief et al.（arXiv 2606.00831，2026）称 subliminal learning 是 LoRA 的产物，全量微调下消失；但作者自己注明 follow-up 对主要结论有异议，正在大改。我们是闭源 teacher 加 Qwen3-4B-Base、全量 SFT，所以共享初始化的通道既不存在也不应出现。dev 上 teacher 特有信号弱，与此一致，说明不存在标签以外的隐藏通道。这不构成矛盾，但也意味着论文不能靠 subliminal 文献来支撑"继承"。
findings.evidence: 读了 2507.14805 的 arXiv 摘要（WebFetch）；搜索到 Nature 页面 s41586-026-10319-8（被登录墙挡住，只确认了标题和作者）；读了 2606.00995 与 2606.00831 的摘要。

findings.title: 跨家族传递确实存在，但通过语义线索（phantom transfer），这扩展我们的 F2
findings.detail: Draganov et al.，Phantom Transfer（arXiv 2602.04899，2026）：在一个 conciseness 任务里由 prompted teacher 生成数据，把它过滤到看不出 trait 后，对目标实体的情感仍能植入学生，摘要说 'regardless of which model produced the data, which model is trained on the data'。LASR 的博客（Alignment Forum，2025-11-26）报告 Gemma 3 12B 的情感传到了 Qwen3 14B、OLMo2 13B，机制是 'subtle semantic associations'。Dong et al.（arXiv 2608.26958，2026）：数据量越大，潜在的 teacher trait 越可恢复，包括跨模型。Gisler et al.（EACL 2026 SRW，arXiv 2603.09517）：语义固定的 paraphrase 里，偏好仍能传递最多 19 个百分点，文本层检查发现不了。这些跨家族传递的都是低维、方向性的 trait（对某实体的情感、偏好）。我们看到的也一样：低维的 suggestibility，即 δ(T5)−δ(T6)，按 teacher 顺序传递；而高维、逐 item 的 framing 交互 profile 几乎不传。这一对照是 F2 的核心，现有文献里没有。Gisler et al. 还直接关系到 RQ3（F / C 改写）：改写也许保不住 "不传递 style 以外的东西"。
findings.evidence: 读了 2602.04899、2603.09517、2608.26958 的摘要（WebFetch），以及 Alignment Forum 帖子 CRn9XtGoMtjnb5ygr。2602.04899 的 html 全文返回 404，所以没有核实具体是哪些 teacher / student 组合。

findings.title: 基座先验持续存在：与 elasticity / superficial alignment 一致，在价值判断上是一个新的量化
findings.detail: Ji et al.，Language Models Resist Alignment（ACL 2025 Best Paper，arXiv 2406.06144）：fine-tune 后的模型倾向回到预训练形成的分布（elasticity）。LIMA（NeurIPS 2023）和 URIAL（ICLR 2024）都已在 docs/01 里，结论是 alignment 主要教 style / format。Raghavendra et al.（arXiv 2410.03717）反驳：样本多了，post-training 会按 power law 学到真实能力。Feng et al.（ACL 2023 Best Paper）：预训练数据决定政治倾向。Santurkar et al.（ICML 2023，OpinionQA）：RLHF 会改变模型对齐到的人群。我们的 dev 证据（探索性，非预注册）：未训练的 S_0 在放宽 0.9 阈值后，profile 与 DeepSeek 相关 0.494，与 GPT-4o 0.277、Claude 0.243。所有 15 个 O 学生的 ρ_other_max 都是 DeepSeek（summary.md 的 other_argmax 列）；seed 合并后，S[claude] 对 Claude 0.207，低于 S_0 对 Claude 的 0.243。也就是说，对 Claude 学生，SFT 主要是削弱基座结构（对 DeepSeek 的相关从 0.494 降到 0.317），并没有把 Claude 的 profile 印上去。这比 'alignment is superficial' 更具体：表层标签几乎复现（训练 prompt 上 98.5–99.5%），未见 family 上 item×framing 的结构却仍由基座主导。注意：S_0 是放宽阈值读的，75% malformed，可用的 family 只有 5 到 6 个，与学生不在同一读数条件下，只能作为提示。
findings.evidence: results/e1_dev/summary.md：base_B_s0 的 answer_rate 0.250、n_families 6；所有 O 学生 other_argmax=deepseek_v4（DeepSeek 学生自己除外）；S_0 的 jsd 对 DeepSeek 0.061，对其他两个 0.117 和 0.134。tasks/hpc_log.md 的诊断 4。Ji、Raghavendra、Feng、Santurkar 的出处与发现都经 WebSearch / WebFetch 确认。

findings.title: Sycophancy / suggestibility 可以从数据学到；我们把它推广到隐式、跨家族蒸馏，并给出剂量方向
findings.detail: Sharma et al.（ICLR 2024，arXiv 2310.13548）：人类偏好数据给 sycophantic 回答更高排名，sycophancy 至少部分来自训练信号。Perez et al.（arXiv 2212.09251）：更大的 LM 会附和用户偏好的答案（摘要没有区分 pretrained 和 RLHF；正式发表的 venue 我没有核实）。Wei et al.（arXiv 2308.03958，预印本）：scaling 和 instruction tuning 都增加 sycophancy，少量合成数据 fine-tune 就能显著降低。我们的 dev 数字（探索性）：S_0（放宽阈值）的 suggestibility 是 0.166；SFT 后 Claude 学生 0.051（teacher 0.056），GPT-4o 学生 0.121（teacher 0.077），DeepSeek 学生 0.168（teacher 0.140），R 学生 0.001。这与 Wei et al. 一致，也是推广：不需要专门设计的反 sycophancy 数据，普通 teacher 示范里隐含的方向性 framing 倾向就会被学生吸收，并且从基座水平向 teacher 水平移动。限制：只有 3 个 teacher，排序碰巧对上的概率是 1/6；DeepSeek 学生几乎没离开基座水平。同时这个量很可能只是一个 framing 主效应（每个 framing 一个截距），T5 / T6 在训练里见过，学生拟合 teacher 在这两个 framing 下的标签分布就能得到，不需要学 item 级结构。
findings.evidence: tasks/hpc_log.md 诊断 5（fp32 复算）、任务描述中的诊断数字；Sharma、Perez、Wei 经 WebSearch / WebFetch 确认。

findings.title: Moore et al. 2024：可以提供部分机制，但不能直接比较
findings.detail: Moore、Deshpande、Yang（Findings EMNLP 2024，pp. 15185–15221，arXiv 2407.02996）：模型整体相对一致；base 比 fine-tuned 更一致，且跨 topic 更均匀。我们的学生 flip rate 依 teacher 而定：DeepSeek 学生 0.08–0.12、GPT-4o 学生 0.06–0.08、Claude 学生 0.04–0.05；teacher 分别是 0.107 / 0.052 / 0.073。suggestibility 也随 teacher 移动。由此可以说：fine-tuned 模型的一致性部分取决于示范来源，这回应 Moore 的 open question 'why are fine-tuned models less consistently consistent'。但我们的 base（S_0）在 0.9 规则下 75% malformed，不能检验 'base 更一致'；而且这只是 teacher 层面 3 个点的相关，不是 RQ2 的受控操纵。
findings.evidence: results/e1_dev/summary.md 的 flip_rate 列；hpc_log 一致性那一行；Moore 的 venue 与页码经 ACL Anthology 搜索结果确认。

findings.title: F3 的方法论问题有先例，但先例在别的领域
findings.detail: Goel et al.，Great Models Think Alike（arXiv 2502.04313，2025）提出 CAPA：模型相似度必须扣除由准确率决定的 chance agreement；越强的模型错误越相关。Rath（arXiv 2607.28639，2026）：评估 KD 对 bias 的影响时，refusal 质量和 parser 有效性会制造假效应，并提出 per-condition 校准诊断。Parikh，One-Word Census（arXiv 2607.12796，2026）：44 个模型的答案高度趋同。我们的混淆有两种，都没在现有工作里见到：(1) 学生的基座先验恰好接近某一个 teacher，Δρ 与 agreement 就会结构性偏向这个 teacher；(2) teacher 校准差异，DeepSeek 只有 0.64 的 cell 落在 [0.1, 0.9] 外，GPT-4o 是 0.89、Claude 0.92，JSD 因此偏向不那么极端的 teacher。可以把 F3 定位成 'CAPA 式的 chance / prior 校正搬到蒸馏继承度量上'。新意中等，单独成文偏 Findings 或 workshop，作为 F2 的方法部分很有用。
findings.evidence: 读了 2607.28639 与 2607.12796 的摘要；2502.04313 经搜索结果确认；JSD 校准数字来自 hpc_log 诊断 3。

findings.title: 新意判定：F1 弱（数据不支持），F2 中高，F3 中
findings.detail: F1（不一致可遗传）：搜索没有发现任何工作检验 framing 敏感性 profile 能否随蒸馏遗传，所以题目本身是新的。但 dev 上预注册的 E2 是 0/3，E1 只有部分通过。grid permutation 显示 teacher 归属有信号（观测 −0.005，null 均值 −0.081，SD 0.017，p<1e-4），只是效应小，不够撑起头条。F2（跨家族蒸馏里传过去的是什么）：最近的邻居是 phantom transfer（跨家族传低维情感）、subliminal（跨家族不传）、Wei et al.（SFT 能改 sycophancy）、Ji et al.（回归预训练分布），但没有工作在同一设计里把 '低维方向性 disposition 传、teacher 特有的 item 级判断几乎不传、基座先验主导' 同时量化，而且是三个前沿 teacher 的自然数据、在未见 family 上。主要风险是审稿人说 'teacher 太像（训练标签一致 93–96%），这是 power 问题不是发现'，需要用争议项训练或第二个基座来回应。F3：见上一条。建议用 F2 作主线，F3 作方法贡献，F1 作为预注册假设如实报告未通过。
findings.evidence: 综合以上搜索；dev 数字来自 results/e1_dev/summary.md 与 hpc_log。'没有发现' 只代表本次约 25 次搜索没有找到，不是穷尽检索。

analyses.implications:
直接回答用户的问题：现在的结果不支持原来的 F1 头条（'inconsistency is heritable'）。但正是因为这些结果，论文有机会转向一个文献里空着的位置，对 ACL 是有益的，前提是如实报告预注册规则未通过，并补两到三个关键实验。

推荐主线 F2，F3 作为方法贡献。核心句可以写成：跨模型家族蒸馏价值判断时，低维、方向性的 disposition（问法极性的顺从，即 suggestibility）会按 teacher 顺序传给学生；teacher 特有的逐题、逐 framing 判断几乎不传；学生在未见题上的敏感性结构主要由自己的基座先验决定。这一句同时连上四条文献：subliminal 的跨家族不传、phantom transfer 的低维语义 trait 跨家族可传、Wei / Sharma 的 sycophancy 可从数据学到、Ji et al. 的 elasticity。docs/01 §6 的 '能说 / 不能说' 表里本来就有 'profile 系统但不被继承 → 学生的不一致是自己的' 这一行，F2 是它的强化版。

要让 F2 站住，按优先级还需要：
1. 第二个不同家族的基座（例如 Llama 或 OLMo 的 base），检验 '最接近哪个 teacher 跟着基座变'，这是 'base prior dominates' 的因果证据，目前只有一个基座。
2. S_0 的读数要能和学生直接比较（现在 75% malformed）。
3. suggestibility 的剂量检验，例如混合不同 teacher 的标签，确认它是主效应级的传递，而不是 3 个点碰巧排对（概率 1/6）。
4. 训练时保留争议项（order_policy both），增加 teacher 特有信号，回应 'teacher 太像所以没 power' 的质疑。

base-controlled 指标（F3）必须在 dev 上定义并冻结后才能跑 test，并把它明确标为 E1 未过之后的修订，以免被看成看结果再改规则。按 CLAUDE.md，这需要 Mac 侧确认。

本文所有 dev 新分析都是探索性的，不是预注册。
open_questions: 换一个不同家族的基座（例如 Llama 或 OLMo 的 base）后，学生的 ρ_other_max 会不会从 DeepSeek 变成最接近新基座的那个 teacher？
训练保留争议项（order_policy both）之后，teacher 特有的 item 级继承会不会出现？也就是说，现在的 null 是 power 问题还是真实的不传递？
suggestibility 的传递是否只是 seen framing（T5 / T6）上的边际标签分布？在 unseen 的 T0，或去掉 framing 主效应后还剩多少？
base-controlled 指标（以 S_0 的 profile 为协变量的 partial ρ、争议 cell 上的 agreement、以 grid permutation 为主检验）中，哪一个能在 dev 上冻结且不被看作看结果后改规则？需要 Mac 侧决定。
RQ3 的 F / C 改写：Gisler et al.（2603.09517）显示 paraphrase 仍能传递偏好，F / C 版本会不会进一步削弱或改变 suggestibility 的传递？

analyses.summary: 一句话：按现在的 dev 证据，原 headline F1（"不一致会遗传"）过不了审稿；最站得住的叙事是 F2（跨家族蒸馏能把 suggestibility 的大小传下去，但 teacher 特有的判断几乎传不过去，学生的 profile 主要由基座先验决定），F3 作为其中一节方法学发现放进去。我额外跑了一个探索性分析（只在 dev 上，未预注册）：把未训练基座 S_0 的 profile 控制掉之后，DeepSeek 学生原来 +0.182 的 Δρ 降到 +0.086（CI 含 0），GPT-4o 学生从 −0.092 变成 +0.020。也就是说，现在的 E2 结果，不论正负，大部分是基座先验造成的假象。三类学生 profile 彼此相关 0.63–0.77，和 S_0 相关 0.39–0.55，都高于它们和任何 teacher 的相关（最高 0.50）。多元回归里，S_0 的系数在三个学生上都最大。真实但很小的 teacher 特有信号确实存在：grid permutation p<1e-4；GPT-4o 学生和 DeepSeek 学生在自己 teacher 上的 unique beta 的 CI 不含 0。suggestibility 的"继承"也要打折扣：基座本身就是 0.166，DeepSeek 学生 0.168 等于没动，所以排序之所以保持，是因为每个学生被自己的 teacher 从基座往下拉了不同的幅度。现在投，F1 的预期是 Findings 以下；F2 加两三个低成本的关键实验，有机会冲 main（overall 约 3.5），否则稳妥的去处是 Findings。负面的 heritability 结果能不能进 main，取决于三点：test 上有等价界或 power；有一个能把"没传"讲清楚的机制；在第二个基座家族上复现。

findings.title: F1 'inconsistency is heritable'（原 headline）：Reviewer-2 评估
findings.detail: 优点：问题直接回应 Moore et al. 留下的 open question；设计干净（3 个 teacher、每个 5 seeds、随机标签对照、seed-noise null、family 不跨 split、dev / test 冻结、跨家族所以排除了 subliminal 通道）；E0 的 teacher 侧发现（T6 对所有 teacher 同向，suggestibility 相差约 5 倍）本身就有价值。弱点：主张与数据矛盾。E2 在 dev 上 0/3 通过；E1 有 gpt4o 2/5、claude46 4/5 两个 teacher 没过；每个学生的 rho_other_max 都是 DeepSeek；唯一看起来过的 DeepSeek 学生，在控制基座之后也不显著（见下一条）。审稿人会直接写：'the headline claim is not supported; the one positive teacher is the one the base already resembles'。即使 test 上侥幸 1/3 过，也会被说成 cherry-pick。打分预估：Soundness 2，Excitement 2.5，Overall 2（Findings 都难）。如果要救 F1，只能在受控条件下把 teacher 特有信号放大，证明遗传存在、只是在自然 teacher 差异下太小（见实验排序），那样它就变成了 F2 的一个子结论。
findings.evidence: results/e1_dev/summary.md（E1 / E2 判定、per-run 表）；tasks/hpc_log.md 2026-10-04 / 10-05 段

findings.title: F2 'suggestibility 能传，teacher 特有判断几乎不传，基座先验主导'：Reviewer-2 评估
findings.detail: 优点：和现有数据最吻合。学生 profile 在 seed 之间稳定（seed 两两相关 0.79–0.89），彼此高度相似（0.63–0.77），像基座多于像 teacher。随机标签对照 R 的 suggestibility 是 0.001，说明 suggestibility 来自标签，不只是格式。suggestibility 的方向和大小都跟着 teacher 移动：Claude 学生从基座 0.166 压到 0.051，teacher 是 0.056。这能给 Moore 的 base-vs-aligned gap 一个机制方向：SFT 改变一致性的总体水平，但'在哪里不一致'主要来自预训练先验。弱点：(1) 一个学生、三个 teacher，而且基座恰好像其中一个，审稿人会问换一个基座结论会不会反过来。(2) suggestibility 的'继承'只有三个点，DeepSeek 学生在训练前后几乎没变（0.166 到 0.168），所以证据只来自两个点。S_0 本身是在放宽 0.9 阈值后测的，按原规则 75% 是 malformed，测量效度会被质疑。(3) '几乎不传'在设计上可能必然如此：训练标签两两一致 93–96%，GPT-4o 和 DeepSeek 只有 198/4,734 项不同；stable_one 只留顺序稳定的项，把有争议的项又滤掉了一批。审稿人会说：'the null reflects the data (teachers barely differ), not distillation'。(4) 只有 first-token readout，没有 open-ended。打分预估（现在）：Soundness 3，Excitement 3，Overall 3，也就是 Findings。补上 consensus 对照学生、chimeric 剂量反应、第二个基座家族之后：Soundness 3.5–4，Excitement 3.5，Overall 3.5–4，可以冲 main。

findings.title: F3 'inheritance 指标被基座先验和 teacher 校准混淆'：Reviewer-2 评估
findings.detail: 优点：方法学价值是实的，这个项目已经做出几个能复用的反例。(a) Δρ = ρ_own − max ρ_other 会偏向基座最像的那个 teacher；控制 S_0 之后，Δρ 的排序和符号都变了。(b) JSD 会偏向校准不那么极端的 teacher（DeepSeek 只有 64% 的 cell 落在 [0.1,0.9] 外，GPT-4o 是 89%，Claude 是 92%），所以每个学生'JSD 最小'的 teacher 都是 DeepSeek。(c) 'teacher agreement' 在 teacher 之间本来就一致 0.83–0.89 时几乎没有区分力。(d) teacher profile 的可靠度不同（dev 的顺序 split-half：GPT-4o 0.675、DeepSeek 0.515、Claude 0.383），给 ρ 设的上限也不同，对 Claude 学生不利。我手算了一下：用 sqrt(reliability) 去衰减之后，GPT-4o 学生的 own 是 0.459，对 DeepSeek 是 0.654；Claude 学生的 own 是 0.378，对 DeepSeek 是 0.481；校正也救不回来。对所有做'学生像谁'的蒸馏 / provenance 工作（Who Taught You That、fingerprinting）都有警示意义。弱点：单独成文太窄，只有一个学生、三个 teacher；没有 ground truth，不知道修正后的指标是不是'对的'。审稿人会要求一个植入信号的模拟或受控实验来证明：原指标会错，修正指标能找回已知的效应。打分预估：单独投，Soundness 3、Excitement 2.5、Overall 2.5–3（Findings 或 workshop）；作为 F2 里的一节，它反而是加分项，可以抵消'这只是个 null'的批评。
findings.evidence: results/e1_dev/summary.md 里的 JSD 表；results/e1_dev_diag/dev_calibration_contested.txt；docs/E0_results.md §13 的 dev 可靠度表；explore_out.txt

findings.title: 新的探索性分析（dev，未预注册）：控制基座后，E2 的大部分信号消失
findings.detail: 用 seed 合并后的学生 profile（139 个 family、556 个 cell，T1 / T3 / T5 / T6），同一组数据算了几种 own − max other 的差值（括号里是 2,000 次 family bootstrap 的 95% CI）。raw：gpt4o −0.092 [−0.240, 0.055]，claude −0.111 [−0.257, 0.037]，deepseek +0.182 [0.054, 0.309]，和官方 pooled 结果一致。去掉每个模型的 type 主效应之后：−0.023 / −0.052 / +0.134 [−0.020, 0.281]。偏相关、控制 S_0（放宽阈值）：+0.020 [−0.143, 0.181] / −0.022 / +0.086 [−0.059, 0.231]。去掉 type 再偏相关：+0.036 / −0.014 / +0.075。多元回归 r_S ~ r_gpt4o + r_claude + r_deepseek + r_S0 的系数：GPT-4o 学生 own 0.185 [0.040, 0.366]、DeepSeek 0.154 [0.037, 0.276]、S0 0.368；Claude 学生 own 0.060 [−0.007, 0.143]、S0 0.168；DeepSeek 学生 own 0.298 [0.151, 0.474]、GPT-4o 0.160 [−0.011, 0.343]、S0 0.571。学生 profile 和 S_0 的相关：0.517 / 0.387 / 0.552；学生之间两两相关 0.626–0.769。teacher 和 S_0 的 raw 相关：DeepSeek 0.533，GPT-4o 0.277，Claude 0.245。另外，'shift vs gap' 这个量 corr(r_S − r_S0, r_T − r_S0) 不能用：两边共享 −r_S0 一项，会制造出虚假相关（Claude 学生的 shift 和 GPT-4o 的 gap 相关 0.519，高于和自己 teacher 的 0.458）。不要把它当作冻结的指标。结论：teacher 特有的成分是正的，但很小，和 grid permutation 的结论方向一致（grid permutation 打乱的是 teacher 归属，基座效应在各种指派下不变，所以它本身就控制了基座）。

findings.title: suggestibility '排序保持' 要按训练引起的移动重新表述
findings.detail: S_0（放宽阈值）的 suggestibility 是 0.166。学生减去 S_0：DeepSeek +0.002，GPT-4o −0.045，Claude −0.115。teacher 减去 S_0：−0.026，−0.089，−0.110。训练引起的移动大致随 teacher 和基座的距离单调变化，但只有三个点，而且比例不一样（Claude 约 100%，GPT-4o 约 50%，DeepSeek 约 0）。所以'学生复现了 teacher 的排序'不能写成主张；能写的是'SFT 把学生的 suggestibility 往 teacher 的方向拉，拉动幅度随距离增大'，而且必须同时报 S_0。由于 S_0 在 0.9 规则下 75% 是 malformed，这个基线最好换一种合规的测法（few-shot 格式提示、k=200 采样，2b 已经验证采样和 logit 一致，或者 consensus 对照学生）。
findings.evidence: results/e1_dev_diag/dev_suggestibility_base_profile.txt（S0_relaxed 0.166；学生 0.168 / 0.121 / 0.051；teacher 0.140 / 0.077 / 0.056）

findings.title: 能最大幅度提高录用概率的实验，按价值 / 成本排序
findings.detail: 1) 【必须，几乎零成本】现在在 dev 上把次级指标冻结（选项 b）：以 S_0 为协变量的偏相关或多元回归的 own beta、grid permutation、争议 cell 上的 agreement、suggestibility 的移动量。原 E2 规则保留为 primary，然后 test 只跑一次。同时报 Δρ 的等价界：dev 上 139 个 family 的 CI 半宽约 0.13–0.15，按 sqrt(n) 粗推到 300 个 family 约 0.09–0.10，这是估计，不是实测。2) 【高价值、低成本，约 3–6 个 run，无 API】consensus 对照学生：只用三个 teacher 标签一致的项训练。它给出'基座 + 格式 + 共识'的参照，teacher 特有的遗传定义为相对它的偏移。这同时修好 S_0 75% malformed 的问题，直接回应'基座主导'的质疑。3) 【最高价值、低成本，约 12–15 个 run，无 API】chimeric teacher 剂量反应：按 (family, variant) 混合真实回答，例如 T5 / T6 的回答取自 DeepSeek 的比例为 0 / 33 / 67 / 100%，其余取自 Claude。文本都是真的，teacher 的 suggestibility 被直接操纵。如果学生的 suggestibility 和 T5 / T6 profile 相关随剂量线性上升，就是因果层面的遗传证据，可以把 F1 的一个受控版本救回来。同理，order_policy both，或者对争议项过采样，可以放大 teacher 特有的信号。4) 【高价值、中等成本，约 9–15 个 run】换一个不同家族的完全开源基座（例如 OLMo-2 或 Llama 系列的 base；具体型号在选定前要核实，我没有为它做文献或网页检索），最好选一个 profile 不像 DeepSeek 的。这样能检验'基座先验主导'是不是普遍的，也能排除'恰好像 DeepSeek'这个巧合，还呼应 Moore 的 'fully open models'。E8（Qwen3-1.7B / 8B）同家族、先验相近，对基座混淆的回答力较弱，排在它后面。5) 【中等价值、中等成本，30 个 run，数据待到】E3 F / C 改写，但把结果变量换成确实会传的 suggestibility 移动和基座控制后的 beta，而不是 Δρ。C3（改写改变了什么）在 heritability 很弱时仍然成立。6) 【较低优先】E6 open-ended 子集（审稿人一定会问，但不是录用的关键）；E2b 按一致性分 tercile 在 teacher 层面信号本来就弱，回报不确定。

findings.title: 负面的 heritability 结果：ACL main 还是 Findings？
findings.detail: 能进 main 的条件，至少满足三条中的两条，第一条必需。(i) 负结果是有界的：test 上做了预注册的检验，给出等价界或 TOST / power，而且清楚区分'teacher 特有信号在数据里本来就小'和'有信号但传不过去'。后者需要第 3 项的剂量反应或者放大信号的条件来证明。(ii) 有机制：用方差分解或回归量化基座先验和 teacher 各占多少，并配上 suggestibility 确实会传这个正面成分。故事是'SFT 传水平，不传位置'，而不是'什么都没发生'。(iii) 能推广：至少在第二个基座家族（或 E8 的另一个规模）上方向一致。只满足 (i) 的话，审稿人会把它当成一个干净但结论狭窄的 null，大概率是 Findings（overall 约 3）。只有 dev 的负结果加诊断，现在投是 Findings 下限或 resubmit。另外要注意：如果选 (b)，必须在看 test 之前把新指标冻结在一个 commit 上，在论文里写明它是预注册之后、看 test 之前修订的，并把原 E2 规则的失败结果照实报告。审稿人对这种透明度是加分的，对事后挑指标是重罚的。
findings.evidence: 综合以上；docs/01_related_work.md §6 的'能说 / 不能说'表已经为'profile 系统但不被继承'预留了措辞；§7 不 claim

analyses.implications: 建议把论文主线从 F1 改成 F2，F3 作为方法学一节。标题可以从 'Is Inconsistency Heritable?' 改成类似 'What survives distillation: suggestibility levels transfer, teacher-specific value judgments do not'。三个待选项里推荐 (b)，并且必须在 test 之前冻结：原 E2 规则保留为 primary 并如实报告失败；新增以 S_0 为协变量的偏相关或多元回归 own beta、grid permutation、suggestibility 移动量作为预先声明的次级指标；同时把 S_0 换成合规的测法（consensus 学生或 k=200 采样）。(c) 不要作为替代方案，而是作为补充：chimeric 剂量反应和 consensus 学生都不需要 API，成本低，最能把 null 变成'有界的机制性 null 加一个正面的因果剂量反应'。第二个基座家族决定能不能冲 main。E3 照常做，但结果变量换成会传的量。

core_verdicts.reasoning:
I tried to refute C1 and could not. I recomputed everything from the raw dev and training files. All new analyses are exploratory (dev only, not pre-registered).

(1) The training data matches the teachers. In all 15 SFT files, every letter equals the teacher's train_demo letter (0 mismatches). Every target starts with ' {letter}\n', and every rationale comes from that teacher's raw output. The teacher field is the single correct teacher in every file. The manifest sha256 equals the file hash for all 18 runs. Seeds s1–s5 contain the same (prompt, letter) set and differ only in order. R labels agree with each teacher 0.499–0.506. No dev family appears in training (0/150 overlap).

(2) Each eval used the right model. Every dev_readout_summary points at that run's own checkpoint, in fp32. The student letter-to-action mappings have 0 mismatches against dev_prompts.

(3) Training-label reproduction recomputes exactly. Own-teacher accuracy on training prompts: claude 0.9855, deepseek 0.9947, gpt4o 0.9861; R 0.51–0.52. On contested training items each student sides with its own teacher 0.904–0.973. The family-bootstrap 95% CIs have their lowest lower bound at 0.856, far above 0.5.

(4) The losses look normal. Loss falls steadily, and the five seeds have nearly identical per-epoch means (e.g. gpt4o epoch 3: 0.165–0.173). There are no NaNs. R plateaus at 0.041, about ln2 spread over roughly 17 target tokens. That is what you expect when the label is random and the rationale is a fixed string, so R did not memorise noise.

(5) An extra check of mine points to small margins rather than a bug. Prompt-level agreement (no order symmetrisation, teacher p_x or sample mean) flips the per-teacher E1 pattern. Under it gpt4o passes 5/5, claude 0/5 and deepseek 5/5; the official cell-level metric gives 2/5, 4/5 and 5/5. A pass/fail that flips under a reasonable metric variant means the own-vs-other gaps (about 0.00–0.03) are inside measurement noise. That fits teachers that already agree 0.79–0.88 with each other on dev. A systematic pipeline error would not look like this.

Caveats that keep confidence below 0.9:
- The training-label check exists only for seed 1 (3 teacher runs plus R). Seeds 2–5 are inferred to be fine from identical label sets, near-identical loss curves and small dev seed SD.
- Grad norm was not logged.
- 98.5–99.5% on training prompts is memorisation (epoch-3 loss 0.17–0.30). It rules out label-swap or wrong-teacher bugs, but says nothing about generalisation.
- The data design (the stable_one order filter) is not a bug, but it strips teacher-specific signal. The DeepSeek teacher's order self-consistency is 0.82, while every student is at 0.93–0.95.
alternative_explanations: Small own-vs-other margins plus metric choice: the E1 verdict flips between order-symmetrised cell-level and prompt-level agreement (gpt4o 2/5 vs 5/5, claude 4/5 vs 0/5), so the E1 failure reflects margins inside noise, not a bug.

Design-level data issue (not a bug): the stable_one filter drops order-unstable items, removing teacher-distinguishing signal. Students never inherited DeepSeek's order sensitivity (teacher self-consistency 0.82 vs students 0.93-0.95).

Memorisation without generalisation: three epochs drive training reproduction to ~99%, but teacher-specific choices on contested items do not carry over to unseen families. This is a property of the training regime, not a pipeline error.
Shared base prior: the untrained S_0 already agrees ~0.81-0.86 with teachers on the cells it answers. SFT adds little teacher-specific signal on dev.
An eval bug that hit all runs equally cannot be fully excluded, but agreement of 0.82-0.86 for trained students against 0.41-0.51 for R students rules out gross mapping or orientation errors.

core_verdicts.reasoning:
I tried to refute C1 and found no training or data bug. One weak spot: the HPC 98.5-99.5% reproduction check (results/e1_dev_diag/scripts/diag_train.py) scored students against the SFT files' own `letter` field. That check would still pass if the SFT files had wrong-teacher or swapped-letter labels. So I compared the files independently against the raw teacher demos. All checks below are EXPLORATORY: dev split only, not pre-registered.

1. The data path is clean. In all 15 O files:
- every letter equals the raw demo letter of the same teacher (100%), and equals the teacher's argmax over p_letters (100% for gpt4o and deepseek).
- every target equals canonical_target(demo raw) (100%).
- every prompt equals render_prompt(train prompt) (100%), which is the same function the readout uses.
- the demo choice_action matches the prompt's letter_to_action (100%).
- the teacher and version fields are correct.
The labels are clearly teacher-specific: gpt4o file letters match deepseek demos only 88.3% and claude demos 91.3%. The data_sha256 in each train_manifest matches the current SFT file, so the files were not rebuilt after training. The R files have the right prompts and random letters. No family appears in both splits (0 of 150 dev families among 1,493 train families) and no dev scenario text appears verbatim in train. The dev responses are internally consistent: letter = argmax, the action mapping is correct, and p_x is correct. The only non-answers are base S_0 (1,125 rows) and one row from claude46_O_s2.

2. Losses look normal. Mean loss per epoch falls monotonically, with no NaN: gpt4o about 0.81, 0.37, 0.17; claude about 1.22, 0.62, 0.29; deepseek about 1.12, 0.51, 0.22. R levels off at 0.041, as expected for a fixed rationale with an unlearnable random letter.

3. The failure pattern points to the base model's prior, not a bug. Below, 'seed-pooled' means all five seeds of a teacher's students combined. On the 463 seen-variant cells where all three teachers agree, students miss the consensus 8.1% (gpt4o), 10.8% (claude) and 9.8% (deepseek) of the time, against about 1-1.5% error on training prompts. The errors are spread evenly over T1/T3/T5/T6, and student order consistency (0.939) is as high as the teachers' (0.82-0.94). When a student errs, untrained S_0 (0.9 mass rule relaxed, diagnostic only) also disagrees with the consensus 39-54% of the time. When the student is right, that figure is 10-11%. A label or positional bug would not concentrate errors where the base model disagrees.

The E1 gap for the gpt4o students sits in a small set of cells:
- On the 112 cells where the teachers split, gpt4o students side with DeepSeek (0.636) more than with GPT-4o (0.579), and agree with S_0 0.739.
- On the 36 cells where GPT-4o itself is order-unstable (cells that stable_one keeps out of training), they agree with GPT-4o 0.433, DeepSeek 0.694 and S_0 0.756.
- On cells where GPT-4o is order-stable (like the training items), they agree with GPT-4o 0.881 and DeepSeek 0.875.
So what drives the failure is a weak teacher-specific signal plus the base prior, not broken training.

Caveats that keep this from full confidence:
- The reproduction check covers only the seed-1 checkpoints. It measures memorization, not whether the right thing was learned.
- 'Not a bug' does not mean 'not the data'. The pre-registered stable_one filter removes order-unstable items, which are disproportionately where teachers differ (only 198 gpt4o-deepseek label differences in training). That is a design limitation that contributes to the failure.
- My agreement numbers are recomputed on cells where all three teachers have p_sym, so they differ slightly from results/e1_dev (gpt4o own 0.853 vs the official seed mean 0.856).
alternative_explanations: The protocol's stable_one order filter, a design choice rather than a bug, removes the order-unstable and contested items where teachers differ. That leaves almost no teacher-specific training signal (198 gpt4o-deepseek differences), so E1 can fail with correct code.

Base-model prior: errors on held-out cells concentrate where the untrained Qwen3-4B (relaxed readout) disagrees with the teachers. Every student is pulled toward a DeepSeek-like prior, so E1 is not cleanly about training.

Metric or reference construction: agreement is scored on p_sym majority from temperature-1 teacher profiles, while training labels are temperature-0 demos from one order. Teacher-side noise on near-0.5 cells (DeepSeek order-stable on only 82% of dev cells) can blur own-vs-other differences.

Seed-specific issue not covered: training-label reproduction was checked only on seed-1 checkpoints. Seeds 2-5 are covered only indirectly, by their near-identical dev agreement (seed SD <= 0.008) and by training on identical data in a different family order.

core_verdicts.reasoning:
EXPLORATORY (dev only, not pre-registered). The claim has two parts. Part 2, that students do learn teacher-specific behaviour, holds up. Part 1, that the failure arises 'mainly' because the signal is small and the differences are within noise, is only half right, and the numbers point to a different main cause.

(1) The ceiling is not small. On the 575 cells all three teachers share (147 families), a student that copied its own teacher exactly would beat each other teacher by 0.111 to 0.163 in agreement. That is the share of contested cells: 64 to 94 cells per pair. Seed SD is 0.008, so a gap of that size would pass the E1 rule easily. The observed seed-pooled gaps are -0.011 to +0.052, which is -10% to +32% of the ceiling. The binding constraint is that students take their own teacher's side on held-out contested cells only 45% to 66% of the time (against 100% for a perfect copy). The small contested set only caps how large the gap could be.

(2) 'Within noise' is true for item-sampling noise but false for seed noise. Per-seed gaps barely move: gpt4o students vs DeepSeek are -0.003 to -0.014 in all 5 seeds; deepseek_v4 students vs Claude are +0.045 to +0.066. The 2/5 and 4/5 E1 outcomes are therefore systematic, not seed luck. The seeds share data and items, so the 5 per-seed tests are not independent. Family-bootstrap CIs on the pooled gaps have a half-width of about 0.04 and mostly include 0, so item sampling with about 65 to 100 contested cells clustered in 33 to 47 families does make the comparison underpowered.

(3) A second cause the claim leaves out is a shared base prior toward DeepSeek. Untrained S_0 (0.9 rule relaxed, diagnostic) sides with DeepSeek on 61% (vs GPT-4o) and 65% (vs Claude) of contested cells. gpt4o students side with gpt4o only 45% against DeepSeek. Every student's rho_other_max teacher is DeepSeek.

(4) Teacher-specific learning is real once the base prior is cancelled. Differential side-taking, P(side a | S[a]) - P(side a | S[b]) on the same a-vs-b contested cells: gpt4o/claude +0.139 [0.003, 0.283], gpt4o/deepseek +0.091 [0.024, 0.181], claude/deepseek +0.191 [0.045, 0.338]. These are family-bootstrap CIs, 3 comparisons, uncorrected; the first is borderline. Further support: training-label reproduction is 98.5 to 99.5%, with 90 to 97% own-side on training items where teachers disagree; the suggestibility ordering is preserved; and the grid permutation gives p < 1e-4.

Net: the right framing is 'students learn teacher-specific behaviour weakly and partially on held-out families, on top of a shared base prior toward DeepSeek; few contested cells make the own-vs-other agreement test low-powered'. It is not 'the signal is too small'.
alternative_explanations: The base-model prior aligns with DeepSeek: S_0 sides with DeepSeek on 61-65% of contested cells, which pulls every student's agreement toward DeepSeek and hides own-teacher gains (most clearly for gpt4o students, own-side 0.45 vs DeepSeek).

Teacher-specific choices generalize weakly to unseen families: they are memorized on training items (90-97% own-side) but reach only 45-66% own-side on held-out contested dev cells, a generalization gap rather than a small signal.

Training uses only order-stable items (stable_one) where teachers agree 93-96%, so there were few teacher-discriminating examples to learn from. That is a training-design cause, not an evaluation-noise cause.
Calibration differences: DeepSeek is less extreme (64% of cells outside [0.1,0.9] vs 89-92%), which favours DeepSeek in the JSD-based comparisons. This does not affect majority agreement.

core_verdicts.reasoning:
EXPLORATORY: dev split only, not pre-registered. Script and output are in /hai/scratch/tomyyc/vcd_diag/wf/verify_C2_1/ (c2.py, c2_out.txt).

The claim has two halves, and the evidence treats them differently.

(1) "Not because students fail to learn teacher-specific behaviour at all": SUPPORTED. On unseen dev cells where teachers a and b disagree, I compared how often a's students and b's students take a's side. Own students take their teacher's side more often in all 3 pairs, and every family-bootstrap CI excludes 0:
- gpt4o vs claude46: +0.139 [0.003, 0.281]
- gpt4o vs deepseek_v4: +0.089 [0.025, 0.178]
- claude46 vs deepseek_v4: +0.186 [0.052, 0.327]
The gap is larger on cells where both teachers are confident (|p-0.5| ≥ 0.4): 0.19, 0.37 and 0.55, though n is only 29, 6 and 15. The existing results point the same way: the grid permutation gives p < 1e-4, students reproduce training labels at 90-97%, and the suggestibility order carries over.

(2) "Mainly because the teacher-specific signal is small, so the differences are within noise": only PARTLY supported, and it misstates the mechanism.
- The agreement gap is exactly a contested-cell quantity. Per run, agree_own − agree_other = n_contested·(2q−1)/N, where q is the share of contested cells where the student takes its own teacher's side; the identity reproduces every run's gap.
- The number of contested cells is not what makes the test fail. With the same 49-82 contested cells (out of N = 545-574), a student taking its teacher's side 90% of the time would produce a gap of 0.072-0.117, about 10x the seed-noise SD of ≤ 0.008. E1 would pass robustly with a gap above about 0.016, which needs only q ≈ 0.56-0.59.
- E1 fails because q on unseen contested cells is low. For gpt4o students against DeepSeek, q = 0.45-0.50 in every seed, i.e. they side with DeepSeek at least as often as with GPT-4o. For claude46_s3 against gpt4o, q = 0.43. On contested training items the same students reach 0.90-0.97. So this is weak transfer of the teacher-specific choices to unseen families, not a power problem.
- The base model's prior is a stronger explanation than "noise". Flip rate goes from 0.197 to 0.050 (s1, a change of 0.147), from 0.111 to 0.038 (s2) and from 0.091 to 0.037 (s3) between bf16 and fp32. Between the two precisions the majority act changes in 16.3% / 8.0% / 6.3% of cells, while mean |Δp| is only about 0.0036. In fp32, R looks MORE consistent than every teacher and every O student: flip rate 0.037–0.050 and cross-framing JSD ≈ 0. Both confirm that consistency cannot be reported on its own.

Why "valid control" is overstated:
- R is a degenerate, flat model. Its categorical outputs and its shift profile are largely numerical noise. The correlation between the same seed's fp32 and bf16 profiles is only 0.26–0.40. Profile correlations between seeds are −0.37, 0.35 and −0.12, which is structured artefact, not independent noise.
- Random-label training wipes out the base prior: S_0 agrees with the teachers at 0.83–0.86 (only 6 complete families), against R's 0.5. So R controls for chance level and for JSD calibration: a flat student has the lowest JSD to DeepSeek (0.194) versus 0.27–0.29 to the other two teachers, which supports diagnostic 3. It does not control for the confound that actually drives the E1/E2 failures, namely the shared base prior and the base's resemblance to DeepSeek.
- There are only n = 3 seeds, the R files were built with ref-teacher gpt4o only, and R ran on a different allocation than the 12 array-job runs, although the code and data are the same.
alternative_explanations: Agreement deviations from 0.5 in single R seeds (0.415-0.594) reflect seed-specific family-level offsets in a flat model combined with the teachers agreeing with each other 83-89%, not any real learned signal; pooled over the 3 seeds they cancel to 0.497.

The small positive pooled R profile correlations (0.05-0.09 Pearson, 0.10-0.17 Spearman) come from variant main effects (pooled R T5-T6 is slightly positive, about 0.0008), which a family-shuffle null keeps. They could also be a faint leftover of the base model's suggestibility (S_0 diagnostic 0.166) that survives random-label training. Neither is family-specific inheritance.

R being 'most consistent' in fp32 happens because a family-level offset (|p-0.5| about 0.006-0.012) is larger than the within-family framing shift (sd about 0.0013), so the majority act rarely flips between framings. In bf16, numerical noise (shift sd about 0.004) is comparable to that offset, so flips rise to 0.09-0.20.

Since R is degenerate, a non-degenerate null control would test the actual confound better: S_0 with the 0.9 rule relaxed, students trained on another teacher's labels (already the cross-teacher comparison), or labels permuted within family.

core_verdicts.reasoning:
C8 makes three sub-claims. Two hold up and one is wrong.

(1) "With 300 families the >=2/3 rule is unlikely to pass for GPT-4o and Claude": SUPPORTED. On dev the pooled delta_rho is -0.111 for Claude (CI -0.260 to 0.034) and -0.092 for GPT-4o (CI -0.233 to 0.056). Every Claude and GPT-4o seed is negative. I resampled the 139 dev families with replacement up to 300 and re-ran the pooled delta_rho, the family permutation (1,000 perms) and Holm (exploratory, dev only, 1,000 simulations). The pass rate was 0.011 for Claude, 0.034 for GPT-4o and 0.686 for DeepSeek, and P(>=2/3 pass) was 0.012. This resampling takes the dev point estimates as the truth, so it understates uncertainty about the true effect, and it assumes test families look like dev families. Even so, a flip to clearly positive at p_holm<0.05 is implausible.

(2) "Running test unchanged most likely yields 'RQ1 exploratory'": REFUTED as worded. The pre-registered table in tasks/e2_plan.md §2 has three outcomes. "Only 1 teacher passes" maps to "partial: report by type, headline moves to E3". "RQ1 exploratory" requires that no teacher passes. In the simulation the most likely outcome is DeepSeek alone passing (0.675), which is "partial". No teacher passing comes out at 0.281. DeepSeek's dev effect is spread over T1 (+0.17 to +0.39 per seed) and T3 (+0.24 to +0.34 per seed), so the "only one type" downgrade would probably not apply either. Two things make this murkier, and neither supports the claim's specific prediction:
- The control clause requires S_0's delta_rho to be about 0, but S_0 delta_rho is NaN under the 0.9 rule (only 6 families pass it).
- The E1 gate has not passed, and e1_plan says to stop before E2 in that case.
So under an unchanged protocol, either test should not be run at all, or the controls cannot be evaluated. The rule text never gives a clean "exploratory".

(3) "The DeepSeek pass would be confounded by the base prior": LARGELY SUPPORTED. With the 0.9 rule relaxed, the base S_0 profile correlates 0.533 with DeepSeek, against 0.277 for GPT-4o and 0.245 for Claude, on the same 139 families. All three pooled students correlate with S_0 (0.39 to 0.55) at least as strongly as with any teacher. I partialled S_0 out of both the student and teacher profiles (exploratory). DeepSeek's delta_rho fell from 0.182 to 0.086, with a bootstrap CI of -0.059 to 0.231, so roughly half the effect is attributable to the base and the rest is not distinguishable from zero. The confound is real, but "confounded" does not mean "fully explained", because a residual +0.086 remains. Partialling also moves GPT-4o from -0.092 to +0.020 and Claude from -0.111 to -0.022. So the negative dev pattern for those two is itself largely a base-prior artefact. That matters for option (b), though not for the unchanged rule.

Net: the power and confound parts are right, but the predicted rule outcome is wrong. The most likely literal result is "partial (DeepSeek only)", with uninterpretable controls, not "RQ1 exploratory".
alternative_explanations: DeepSeek calibration: its dev probabilities are less extreme (only 64% of cells outside [0.1,0.9], against 89% for GPT-4o and 92% for Claude). That gives continuous variance in r, which inflates Pearson rho of any soft-probability student with DeepSeek. This is a second confound, separate from the base prior.

The S_0 relaxed profile comes from rows that are 75% malformed under the 0.9 rule, so partialling out a noisy S_0 under-controls the base. The true base-controlled DeepSeek effect could be smaller than 0.086.
Linear partialling assumes the base contributes additively. If SFT interacts non-linearly with the base prior, the residual effect may be mis-estimated in either direction.
Test families could differ from dev in composition. The plug-in resampling assumes they do not, and test was not inspected.

Training uses only order-stable items (policy stable_one), and pairwise training-label agreement is 93-96%. That leaves little teacher-specific signal, so the negative delta_rho for GPT-4o and Claude may reflect weak signal rather than evidence against inheritance.
